messages.subject: mclapply and active hours
parts:
Hi,

I've deployed an app and we are evaluating the service of potentially hosting our application, one of the key things I'm interested in how quickly the number of active hours rack up, currently our app uses mclapply to get run times down from 12 seconds for a calculation to about 4 which makes things much more responsive.  However it dose so by using 8 cores, the rest of the code is single threaded, my concern is will this mean that 8 active threads will spin for 5 mins (I've lowered the default time out to five) meaning that each hit of the app even if used only for 1 min will consume 40 mins of active time?  Or is it simply counting the number of mins the parent single core shiny process is running for?

Matt.

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] mclapply and active hours
parts:
Hi Matt,
The active hours are measured on the instance level, your 5 minute timeout is applying on the instance level as well.  Let us say you have 10 people hitting your application in an hour for 5 minutes each, but you have only configured one instance (an instance can have more than one R worker process).  Then your account will consume 60 minutes.  It might be helpful to read this article to make sure the notion of instances and workers are clear.  I will add an item to our backlog to do a better job explaining how active hours are tracked.

https://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps-io-performance-tuning/

Best,
Tareef
